html:
A state proclaimed in southeastern Nigeria on 30 May 1967 by Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu, after two coups in 1966 and the killing of thousands of Igbo in the north.

The federal government under Yakubu Gowon went to war to end the secession in July 1967. Biafra, cut off by a blockade, lost territory steadily, and the famine that followed killed between half a million and two million people, by differing estimates. Biafra surrendered on 15 January 1970. Gowon declared "no victor, no vanquished", and the Igbo were taken back into Nigeria, but many lost their property. The war is the subject of Adichie's Half of a Yellow Sun, and calls for Biafra still recur. See also the Igbo.
